answer: Trust grows like a vine: each new identity starts on a low ridge with a 100-unit bond and a tiny trade cap, and every epoch 5% of its trades are randomly spot-audited by three independent auditors who check goods really changed hands with a real counterparty. Fake identities fail because their trades just echo between their own accounts, so one failed audit forfeits the 100-unit bond and prunes the entire linked vine at once. An attacker running 50 fakes must post 5,000 units and still loses it all to a single audit, while honest agents keep their bond and climb the ridge.
